questions.title: Kendall tau-a under continuous independence
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in M. G. Kendall, A New Measure of Rank Correlation, Biometrika 30(1-2) (1938), 81-93, DOI 10.1093/biomet/30.1-2.81. For n>=3 paired observations (X_i,Y_i) with no ties in either coordinate, define the pair score h_ij=sign((X_i-X_j)(Y_i-Y_j)), the concordance score S=sum_{i<j} h_ij=C-D, and tau_a=2S/[n(n-1)]. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation. Under independent continuous marginals, derive E(tau_a)=0 and Var(tau_a)=2(2n+5)/[9n(n-1)] by accounting for identical, overlapping, and disjoint index pairs, and justify the standardized asymptotic normal test without presenting the approximation as an exact finite-sample law. Establish pair-count identities, exchange symmetry, observation-order invariance, invariance under strictly increasing coordinate transformations, sign reversal under a strictly decreasing transformation of exactly one coordinate, and the perfect agreement/disagreement boundaries. State precisely why ties, dependence, small-sample discreteness, and one-sided alternatives fall outside the frozen claim. Keep active and rejected derivations visibly distinct and disclose unresolved gaps. The required model-authored artifact is est_kendall_tau_a and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen public contract. Exploratory Python or R may enumerate permutations and test identities. A separately frozen confirmatory experiment draws independent continuous pairs from several marginal families and checks the exact null mean and variance plus large-sample normal calibration using predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

source.title: A New Measure of Rank Correlation
source.author: M. G. Kendall

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.meaning: The first coordinate of n paired observations.
request_fields.shape: one-dimensional array of n>=3 distinct finite JSON numbers
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, repeated values, non-arrays, and lengths below three.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.meaning: The second coordinate of the same n paired observations.
request_fields.shape: one-dimensional array of exactly n distinct finite JSON numbers
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, repeated values, non-arrays, and every length unequal to x.

response_fields.name: n
response_fields.meaning: The admitted number of paired observations.

response_fields.name: total_pairs
response_fields.meaning: The number of unordered observation pairs.

response_fields.name: concordant_pairs
response_fields.meaning: The number C of pairs whose coordinate differences have the same sign.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals total_pairs under perfect increasing agreement.
response_fields.normalization: Each unordered pair is counted once.

response_fields.name: discordant_pairs
response_fields.meaning: The number D of pairs whose coordinate differences have opposite signs.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals total_pairs under perfect decreasing agreement.
response_fields.normalization: Each unordered pair is counted once.

response_fields.name: score
response_fields.shape: scalar integer between minus total_pairs and total_pairs
response_fields.edge_cases: Has the same parity as total_pairs.

response_fields.name: tau
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals 1 for perfect agreement and -1 for perfect disagreement.

response_fields.name: null_variance
response_fields.meaning: The exact finite-n variance of tau under independent continuous marginals.
response_fields.edge_cases: This no-ties independence variance is not a tie-corrected variance.

response_fields.name: z_statistic
response_fields.meaning: The standardized tau statistic for the frozen large-sample test.
response_fields.edge_cases: Its finite-sample distribution is discrete and not asserted to be exactly normal.
response_fields.normalization: Exactly tau/sqrt(null_variance), with no continuity correction.

response_fields.name: p_value
response_fields.meaning: The frozen two-sided asymptotic normal p-value for absence of association.
response_fields.edge_cases: It is not an exact permutation p-value and is not one-sided.
response_fields.normalization: Exactly 2 times the standard-normal upper tail at abs(z_statistic).

invariants.meaning: The request is a JSON object with exactly x and y; the response contains exactly the nine declared fields; implicit boolean or string coercion is forbidden.
With no ties, concordant_pairs+discordant_pairs=total_pairs, score=concordant_pairs-discordant_pairs, and tau=score/total_pairs.
Applying the same permutation to x and y leaves every response field unchanged.
Exchanging x and y leaves every response field unchanged.
Applying arbitrary strictly increasing transformations separately to x and y leaves every response field unchanged.

Applying a strictly decreasing transformation to exactly one coordinate swaps concordant and discordant counts, negates score, tau, and z_statistic, and leaves n, total_pairs, null_variance, and the two-sided p_value unchanged.
Common strict ordering gives tau=1; reversing exactly one ordering gives tau=-1.

empirical_claims.meaning: Across each frozen independent continuous DGP, the Monte Carlo mean of tau is compatible with zero under the predeclared uncertainty rule.
Across each frozen independent continuous DGP, the Monte Carlo variance of tau is compatible with 2(2n+5)/[9n(n-1)] under the predeclared uncertainty rule.

For the frozen moderate and large n settings, standardized tau and its two-sided normal p-value are compatible with the declared large-sample normal diagnostics; no exact finite-sample normality is claimed.

Every confirmatory replicate uses the frozen n, independent continuous marginal generators, estimator identity, no-ties admission rule, seed, and two-sided no-continuity-correction normalization fixed before outcomes.
